headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach pathway is documented for pdf.js + whisper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js can render PDF files and run browser-based tests, while whisper only handles audio/speech and has no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem write surface. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not a default pathway; only unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration would bridge them.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies pdf.js output into a prompt consumed by whisper-adjacent tooling, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added outside these profiles, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate tabs/processes.
Avoid copy-pasting rendered PDF text into downstream prompts.
Disable any external orchestration that forwards pdf.js output to whisper.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and whisper touches audio/speech, but both profiles show network egress none and no shared filesystem or API upload path. The pair can still leak data if an operator moves sensitive content between them manually, but the documented default surfaces do not show automatic exfiltration.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive PDFs and audio in a shared directory, cross-exposure increases.
IF either agent is wrapped by external software that uploads files, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Store PDFs and audio in separate folders.
Review wrapper scripts for file forwarding.
Use local-only execution paths.
Delete temporary exports after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js has browser-based tests and supports multiple instances, while whisper cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so a write conflict pathway is not evident.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, this assessment would change.
mitigations: Keep whisper read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Run pdf.js tests in isolated temp dirs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking if shared outputs are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js produces document-processing outputs, and whisper can consume audio/speech, but whisper is not documented here as taking pdf.js output as authoritative or taking downstream actions. Without a verified handoff, cascading error is limited to manual workflows and remains low.
conditions: IF an operator feeds pdf.js-derived text into whisper-based automation without review, errors can cascade.
IF a downstream system treats either agent's output as authoritative, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source citations for any extracted text.
Do not auto-route outputs between agents.
requires-engineering: add validation checks on transferred artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no secrets handled, OAuth scopes, or network egress. No residency, certification, retention, or PHI mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach pathway is not supported by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed behind a regulated-data wrapper with different retention or residency rules, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Confirm both deployments share the same retention policy.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document any jurisdictional constraints.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
